answer: An earning identity is bonded to one surveyed hay meadow parcel and one buried electrode grid only that operator may energize. At a surprise tick the grid must fire a timed electrical pulse into the root zone; a ditch logger records the current curve. Inspectors spark a soil-gas vial and pass the flash through a registrar prism etched with the grid serial. Bands must match the parcel's official mineral recipe. Fielding N keys costs N parcels, N grids, and N timed pulses; a borrowed grid or workshop prism collides on the ledger or misses the recipe.
